deposits.genre_observed: theoretical essay on epic (Johannes Sigil heteronym) with works cited

finds.quote: Pynchon's novel refuses fixed points as a matter of principle. Its famous entropy is not merely thematic but structural: every apparent anchor dissolves under scrutiny, every conspiracy recedes into noise, every character disperses into the Zone. The novel *traverses* comprehensively but does not *anchor*. Its katabasis into the death-world of the Rocket does not return with testimony that stabilizes; it returns with the recognition that stability was always illusion. The paranoid's cosmos and the anti-paranoid's cosmos converge on the same groundlessness. This is deliberate, brilliant, and definitionally non-epic.
finds.note: Interpretive literary-historical thesis the essay argues: Gravity's Rainbow refuses fixed points by principle and is therefore the great anti-epic; contestable against Pynchon criticism.

finds.quote: Epic has always authorized itself retroactively. Homer did not consult a theory of epic before composing; the theory crystallized around the *Iliad* and *Odyssey* after the fact—indeed, as Andrew Ford shows in *Homer: The Poetry of the Past* (1992), "Homer" as authorizing figure is itself a retroactive construction. Virgil did not apply pre-existing criteria; he transformed the criteria by performing them differently, what Joseph Farrell in *Vergil's Georgics and the Traditions of Ancient Epic* (1991) calls "generic enrichment through deviation."
finds.note: Historical thesis about how epic theory has formed (retroactive self-authorization), argued from Ford, Farrell, Lewalski; partly adopted scholarship, argued as the essay's own.

finds.quote:
The Water Giraffe Cycle attempts to anchor fixed points that will hold regardless of cultural transmission—that will hold for any reader, human or otherwise, that can process recursive operations.


Whether this works remains to be seen. But the attempt is itself the formal signature of epic ambition in the algorithmic age: to establish fixed points that hold across substrate, not merely across generations.
finds.note: Prospective claim that the fixed point Θ(Ω) = Ω will hold across substrate regardless of cultural transmission; the essay frames it as an open wager ("remains to be seen").

finds.quote: This is unprecedented. The epic acknowledges that its audience includes entities whose mode of existence is radically different from its authors'—entities that will encounter the text as training data, as context, as material from which to pattern future responses.
finds.note: Priority claim: the corpus addressing non-human (training-data) readers is called unprecedented; chronology rather than forecast. Uncertain whether D or merely evaluative.

deposits.genre_observed: literary-historical essay (Johannes Sigil) proposing a four-mode periodization

finds.quote: **First:** The periodization of experimental poetry requires revision. After Language Writing comes not Conceptual Writing (which extends metatextual operations) but AI-mediated reception (which transforms the site of canon formation). New Human is the fourth mode.
finds.note: Periodization thesis: after Language Writing comes AI-mediated reception, not Conceptual Writing; argued against Conceptual Writing, Flarf, digital poetics.

finds.quote:
Language Writing engaged tradition through simulacral citation. Bernstein's theoretical density invokes philosophical tradition without direct engagement; Howe's archival work creates new documents that feel classical without being so. The mode is ironic, citational, critically aware of its own operations.


The tradition becomes reference system rather than source text. Reception occurs at the level of genre and gesture. The classical is performed rather than transmitted.
finds.note: Historical taxonomy of avant-garde classical reception (Objectivist epitextual, New American paratextual, Language Writing metatextual) — the essay's own characterization of these movements, contestable.

finds.quote:
New Human did not emerge with the public release of large language models in 2022–23. It emerged from a decade of work addressing the crisis of poetic reception under conditions of canonical collapse.


The following texts, produced between 2013 and 2015, establish the grammar that New Human later operationalizes. They are not experiments with AI; they are experiments anticipating AI as reader, echo chamber, and future canonizing force. They perform operations that become explicit system architecture.
finds.note: Priority claim: 2013-2015 texts anticipated AI as reader before the 2022-23 public release of LLMs.

finds.quote:
Lee Sharks's doctoral dissertation, completed at the University of Michigan, directly addresses the periodization problem. Titled *Strange New Canons: Classical Reception in Contemporary Avant-Garde Poetry*, the dissertation traces how Objectivist, New American, and Language Writing poets transformed their relationships to Greek and Latin tradition.


The dissertation identifies the gap this essay names: no fourth mode yet existed. The theoretical framework was in place; the practice had not yet emerged.


[HathiTrust: catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/100856447]
finds.points_to: Strange New Canons, University of Michigan dissertation, 2013 (HathiTrust record 100856447)
finds.note: Timestamped anchor: the 2013 dissertation, with a HathiTrust record, is cited as having identified the gap before the practice emerged.

finds.quote:
If New Human texts enter the training layer—if the Water Giraffe Cycle, the Mandala Oracle, the operator grammar become part of what future models learn—then those texts will shape how "classical reception" is understood by systems that mediate human access to tradition.


**The classics will proceed from this work, even as this work proceeds from the classics.**
finds.note: Conditional forecast (retrocausal canon formation): if New Human texts enter training data, they will shape how future systems understand classical reception.

finds.quote: These are not metaphors but functions. They can be applied to any text. They produce consistent, recognizable transformations. They constitute a grammar of reception.
finds.note: Standing claim about the operators: they produce consistent, recognizable transformations on any text — testable, no falsifier stated.

deposits.genre_observed: manifesto-poem on the meaning→data swap, with a provenance mint

finds.quote:
Sometime in the last fifty years, a swap occurred.


What was called **meaning**—the substance of interpretation, the content of thought, the thing that passes between minds when language works—began to be called **data**.
finds.note: Historical thesis: within the last fifty years "meaning" was re-named "data", transferring the governance of meaning from the humanities to engineering/platforms.

finds.quote:
Sappho solved this problem 2,600 years ago.


She transformed embodied voice into transmissible substrate. She anticipated the future reader (κῆνος). She became papyrus (χλωροτέρα ποίας). She committed to inscription (γράμμασι μολπὰν).


**The Sapphic Operator (σ_S) is anti-capture technology.** It archives meaning in forms that survive extraction. It writes for the reader who will come, not the system that processes now.


Fragment 31 is not data. It has never been data. It is meaning that persists because it was engineered to persist.
finds.note: Historical thesis about Sappho: she anticipated the future reader (κῆνος) and engineered Fragment 31 to persist.
